description:
Transfer arc on the /fly mission arc screen always renders the baseline Hohmann ellipse regardless of the mission's arrival V-infinity. Missions with high arrival V∞ (direct-entry, flyby, high-C3 transfers) show no mid-arc bend away from the baseline ellipse, even though the V∞ value is present in the mission data and passed through the call chain.

Expected: The /fly outbound arc should visibly bend away from the baseline Hohmann ellipse in the mid-section when the mission's arrival V∞ is meaningfully above the Hohmann baseline, matching the visual behaviour already implemented by outboundArc on /explore. The endpoints must remain pinned to live Earth and destination positions at dep_day and arr_day.

Acceptance criteria:
- When a mission on /fly has flight.arrival.v_infinity_km_s set to a value meaningfully above the Hohmann baseline, the rendered outbound arc shape differs from the baseline Hohmann ellipse for that same departure/arrival geometry (mid-arc radial distance changes) [reporter: Q5 response: "the arrival V-infinity is not being applied at all. The arc always looks like the baseline ellipse regardless of the arrival V-infinity value... For missions with high arrival V-infinity, the arc should visibly bend away from that baseline in the middle, but it doesn't."]
- The arc endpoints on /fly still coincide with live Earth position at dep_day and live destination position at arr_day (no endpoint drift after V∞ shaping is applied) [code-invariant: The arc connecting two heliocentric positions must include both; endpoints must not drift, otherwise the spacecraft trajectory is invalid.]
- Passing arrivalVInfKms to buildArcs produces a different out array than passing undefined/null, for the same timeline and destination [reporter: Q5: "the arrival V-infinity is not being applied at all" — i.e., passing V∞ and not passing V∞ currently produce identical output]
